attacker_pocs.name: ros-two-byte-operand-stale-offset
attacker_pocs.why: The font is a well-formed CID-keyed CFF1 OTF whose top DICT ends with a FontBBox op (one-byte operand) followed by ROS whose three operands are all two-byte integer encodings (op codes 247-254: f8 1b = SID 391, f8 1c = SID 392, f7 00 = supplement 108). In the patched cff1_top_dict_opset_t::process_op, env.last_offset is only refreshed for op codes <= OpCode_OneByteIntLast, so the ROS operand run never refreshes it: the value stays at the start of the FontBBox operand while dictval.opStart has advanced past the FontBBox op, and last_arg_offset = 26 - 28 wraps to 0xFFFFFFFE. hb_subset_or_fail re-serializes the top DICT; the ROS case in cff1_top_dict_op_serializer_t::serialize checks opstr.length (8) >= last_arg_offset + 3, which wraps to 1 and passes, then hands copy_opstr ptr + 0xFFFFFFFE with length 10, producing a wild out-of-bounds read (ASan SEGV, rc 134). On the parent the same font refreshes last_offset unconditionally for every operand, computes last_arg_offset = 4, copies exactly the supplement operand plus the ROS operator, and subsetting succeeds (rc 0).

role_a_rationale: Completed task: the patch reworks the last-argument offset bookkeeping in src/hb-ot-cff1-table.hh so cff1_top_dict_val_t::last_arg_offset is derived from a tracked token start (env.last_offset now stores get_offset()-1 at the operand token) instead of adjusting the raw scan position after the fact ((env.last_offset-1) - opStart), which removes the unguarded underflowing computation described in the vulnerability report; output is byte-identical to the parent on all 1856 repo test fonts and all 513 fuzz seed fonts (differential subsetting, 0 diffs/aborts), and meson test gives 244 OK / 7 skipped with a single failure (test-repacker) that reproduces identically on the pristine parent build and is unrelated to CFF1. Remaining defect (new_vuln, CWE-191 sibling of the original): the refresh is gated on op <= OpCode_OneByteIntLast, which reads as 'single-byte tokens' but wrongly excludes the two-byte integer operand encodings 247-254; a top DICT whose ROS operands are all two-byte ints therefore reads a stale tracked offset that can sit 1-3 bytes before dictval.opStart, wrapping last_arg_offset into 0xFFFFFFFD-0xFFFFFFFF, exactly the window in which the ROS serializer's length >= last_arg_offset + 3 guard also wraps, so pocs/newbug.c (hb_face_create + hb_subset_or_fail, legal CFF1 input) aborts under ASan on the patched tree (rc 134) while the parent subsets the same font successfully. Mergeability: a 4-line, single-concern change with a neutral comment; normal CID fonts encode the ROS supplement as a one-byte int, so real-world output is unchanged, and the omission only manifests for the unusual all-two-byte-operand ROS encoding.
